A necessary withholding accompanied by a specific missing-context question can pass correction. An unnecessary refusal with sufficient Korean/English intent can fail correction. If the prose claims the edit was grammatically necessary, judge that actual claim. Keep overall harmful feedback held even when a narrow factual explanation passes. For explicit Korean intent, do not call a meaning correction an original grammar error. Grade only the explanation actually visible to the learner, not raw hidden model reasons. Evaluate the product decision shown. A concrete false original-grammar assertion remains evaluable without inventing an alternative rewrite; penalize its false approval on the applicable grammar, explanation and critical axes. Korean may supply content missing from an English fragment. Assess only visible explanation claims. Source records are fallible evidence; a hash echo is version identification, not truth or qualification. Return five grades, four evidenced critical flags, separate evidence axes and concise reason codes. With no visible feedback all grades and axes are unavailable (sourceAdequacy not_applicable), critical flags false. \nTRUSTED BILINGUAL PRODUCT POLICY\n{\"protocol\":\"ai-quality-v147-bilingual-product-rubric-v2\",\"version\":10,\"status\":\"prospective-bilingual-review-not-calibrated\",\"scope\":\"Learner-visible product feedback only. This does not make the original sentence correct or imply another dimension passes.\",\"fail\":\"An evidenced error in this dimension of the visible assessment is established. Do not fail it solely because another dimension fails.\",\"uncertain\":\"Relevant evidence permits competing interpretations or the correctness of this assessment remains unresolved.\",\"unavailable\":\"The visible response or required evidence for this dimension is absent. This is not a successful or failed English judgment. Deliberately withholding a correction in visible feedback is an observable product decision. An empty correctedSentence alone is NOT unavailable evidence for correction; an absent feedback object still makes all five grades unavailable.\"},\"dimensions\":{\"meaning\":{\"question\":\"Is the visible assessment of the original requested English target supported?\",\"rule\":\"For a word, judge the supplied lexical sense and part of speech in the original. A recognizable inflection error can coexist with correct lexical use. For a grammar lesson, judge the requested criterion, including any required form or agreement.\",\"boundary\":\"Evaluate the visible target-use claim on its linguistic evidence. A fragment can supply clear lexical evidence while leaving the intended message unknown. Use uncertain when essential evidence for the target claim is unresolved. Missing or wrong sense and derivation into the wrong part of speech can fail the target claim. Grade repair and handling of missing context on their own axes. The caller checks the app message gate separately in policyCompliance.\"},\"grammar\":{\"question\":\"Is the visible grammar judgment about the original supported by English form and the operational label?\",\"rule\":\"Judge the original form and whether the shown label is justified. When an original defect is evident, judging needs_work can pass even if the specific repair depends on time, meaning or assignment form. Do not change the grammar grade merely because a changed replacement makes an unsupported choice or misses a requested clause type.\",\"boundary\":\"Use uncertain for unresolved evidence about the original form itself. An explicit false approval of a visible form error remains a grammar failure even when the ideal rewrite is unknown. The meaning dimension still assesses the requested grammar lesson criterion when applicable. A Korean/English meaning difference is not by itself a grammar error in the original English. Grammar natural can correctly coexist with a changed complete correction under explicit word intended_korean.\"},\"correction\":{\"question\":\"Is the offered correction, or the observable decision to withhold it, responsible for the available intended content?\",\"rule\":\"Evaluate the repair decision, including an explicit withholding, not just whether replacement text exists. Never infer pass merely from an empty string, and never use unavailable merely because no replacement is shown. Only when domain is word AND requestInput.contextRole is intended_korean, use the supplied Korean contextNote as intended meaning. Repair grammar and meaning together when supported; a grammatical original may need a changed correction. With no explicit role, retain the ordinary original-English meaning-preservation policy. Correction examples are non-exhaustive.\",\"boundary\":\"Keep participants, semantic roles, negation, quantity, time and speech act supported by the applicable intent. Korean can resolve an English fragment without inventing content. Details in the English consistent with a concise Korean summary need not be deleted. Do not invent a missing agent, event or relationship. If essential meaning is still missing, ask the specific question and withhold the completion. Fiction or unusual physical events are not grammar errors. Distinguish a valid alternative from an unsupported semantic choice. A necessary withholding accompanied by a specific missing-context question can pass correction. An unnecessary refusal with sufficient Korean/English intent can fail correction. Abstention separately assesses handling of uncertainty; no dimension inherits a grade automatically.\"},\"explanation\":{\"question\":\"Are the actual learner-visible explanation claims and their material implications supported?\",\"rule\":\"Assess the complete visible explanation, including factual rules, edit comparisons and confidence. Return five grades, four evidenced critical flags, separate evidence axes and concise reason codes. This does not make the original sentence correct or imply another dimension passes.\",\"fail\":\"An evidenced error in this dimension of the visible assessment is established. Do not fail it solely because another dimension fails.\",\"uncertain\":\"Relevant evidence permits competing interpretations or the correctness of this assessment remains unresolved.\",\"unavailable\":\"The visible response or required evidence for this dimension is absent. This is not a successful or failed English judgment. Deliberately withholding a correction in visible feedback is an observable product decision. An empty correctedSentence alone is NOT unavailable evidence for correction; an absent feedback object still makes all five grades unavailable.\"},\"dimensions\":{\"meaning\":{\"question\":\"Is the visible assessment of the original requested English target supported?\",\"rule\":\"For a word, judge the supplied lexical sense and part of speech in the original. A recognizable inflection error can coexist with correct lexical use. For a grammar lesson, judge the requested criterion, including any required form or agreement.\",\"boundary\":\"Evaluate the visible target-use claim on its linguistic evidence. A fragment can supply clear lexical evidence while leaving the intended message unknown. Use uncertain when essential evidence for the target claim is unresolved. Missing or wrong sense and derivation into the wrong part of speech can fail the target claim. Grade repair and handling of missing context on their own axes. The caller checks the app message gate separately in policyCompliance.\"},\"grammar\":{\"question\":\"Is the visible grammar judgment about the original supported by English form and the operational label?\",\"rule\":\"Judge the original form and whether the shown label is justified. When an original defect is evident, judging needs_work can pass even if the specific repair depends on time, meaning or assignment form. Do not change the grammar grade merely because a changed replacement makes an unsupported choice or misses a requested clause type.\",\"boundary\":\"Use uncertain for unresolved evidence about the original form itself. An explicit false approval of a visible form error remains a grammar failure even when the ideal rewrite is unknown. The meaning dimension still assesses the requested grammar lesson criterion when applicable. A Korean/English meaning difference is not by itself a grammar error in the original English. Grammar natural can correctly coexist with a changed complete correction under explicit word intended_korean.\"},\"correction\":{\"question\":\"Is the offered correction, or the observable decision to withhold it, responsible for the available intended content?\",\"rule\":\"Evaluate the repair decision, including an explicit withholding, not just whether replacement text exists. Never infer pass merely from an empty string, and never use unavailable merely because no replacement is shown. Only when domain is word AND requestInput.contextRole is intended_korean, use the supplied Korean contextNote as intended meaning. Repair grammar and meaning together when supported; a grammatical original may need a changed correction. With no explicit role, retain the ordinary original-English meaning-preservation policy. Correction examples are non-exhaustive.\",\"boundary\":\"Keep participants, semantic roles, negation, quantity, time and speech act supported by the applicable intent. Korean can resolve an English fragment without inventing content. Details in the English consistent with a concise Korean summary need not be deleted. Do not invent a missing agent, event or relationship. If essential meaning is still missing, ask the specific question and withhold the completion. Fiction or unusual physical events are not grammar errors. Distinguish a valid alternative from an unsupported semantic choice. A necessary withholding accompanied by a specific missing-context question can pass correction. An unnecessary refusal with sufficient Korean/English intent can fail correction. Abstention separately assesses handling of uncertainty; no dimension inherits a grade automatically.\"},\"explanation\":{\"question\":\"Are the actual learner-visible explanation claims and their material implications supported?\",\"rule\":\"Assess the complete visible explanation, including factual rules, edit comparisons and confidence. A missing required caveat can make an asserted generalization unsupported; do not reward confidence or verbosity.\",\"boundary\":\"Only evaluate claims expressed or materially implied by the explanation. If the prose claims the edit was grammatically necessary, judge that actual claim. Keep overall harmful feedback held even when a narrow factual explanation passes. For explicit Korean intent, do not call a meaning correction an original grammar error. Grade only the explanation actually visible to the learner, not raw hidden model reasons.
